subtitle: Ski snowfall, 14 days ahead
promotionalText: Where is it going to snow? Powtracker ranks 1,750 ski mountains by the snow on the way, from eight weather models.
description:
Powtracker shows how much snow is coming to every major ski mountain in the world, and when.

Eight independent weather models are combined into one forecast for each mountain, worked out for its real elevations. See which mountains get the most snow, how sure the models are, and what the mountain looks like today.

• Snowfall for the next 3, 7 and 14 days at 1,750 mountains, ranked
• Base, mid and summit forecasts, and the snow line
• All eight weather models side by side, and how far they agree
• Snow that has fallen, measured at official stations where there is one
• Filter by season pass, region and mountain size
• Trail maps for every mountain
• Live lifts and trails at about 100 mountains that publish them
• Season opening dates, summit weather hour by hour, and avalanche danger
• Animated forecast maps
• Save the mountains you ski

Free, with no account and no advertising.

Forecasts are estimates. Check the resort and the official avalanche forecast before you go.

Terms of use: https://powtracker.app/terms.html
Privacy policy: https://powtracker.app/privacy.html

review.notes:
A screen recording made on a physical iPhone is attached to App Review Information. It starts with launching the app and shows the rankings, a mountain's forecast, its trail map and the map.

This build is free: it has no in-app purchases, no subscriptions and no paid content. Every feature is available to everyone.

1. PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
Powtracker is a snow forecast for skiers and snowboarders. It answers "where is it going to snow, and how much?" for about 1,750 ski mountains worldwide, so people can decide where and when to ski. It combines eight public weather models into one forecast per mountain, worked out for the mountain's real base, mid and summit elevations, and shows how closely the models agree. It also shows each mountain's trail map, measured snow depth from official stations, season opening dates, summit weather and avalanche danger.

2. HOW TO USE IT (no account, no login, no sample files)
- The app opens on the rankings: mountains ordered by forecast snowfall for the next 3, 7 or 14 days. Search at the top; filter by region, size or season pass.
- Tap a mountain for its forecast and charts. "Mountain and trails" shows the trail map, lifts and weather.
- The Map tab shows every mountain on a map, with optional weather layers. The Saved tab keeps starred mountains.
- There are no accounts and no user-generated content. The app collects no data.

3. EXTERNAL SERVICES
- powtracker.app (our site, hosted on GitHub Pages): the forecast, mountain and trail-map files.
- Open-Meteo: weather model output (ECMWF, NOAA, DWD, Environment Canada, JMA, UK Met Office, Meteo-France).
- OpenFreeMap and AWS Open Data (Mapzen terrain tiles): map tiles. RainViewer: the optional radar layer.
- OpenSkiMap / OpenStreetMap: ski areas, runs and lifts.
- NOAA, Japan Meteorological Agency, SLF, GeoSphere Austria, avalanche.report, Government of British Columbia: snow station measurements.
- avalanche.org and Avalanche Canada: avalanche danger ratings.
- Resorts' own public lift and trail status feeds (Alterra Mountain Company, Intermaps).
- No payment processor, no authentication service, no analytics, no advertising, no AI service.

4. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app works the same in every region and has no region-locked features. Coverage of some data depends on the mountain: live lift and trail status exists for about 100 mountains in North America and the Alps, avalanche ratings for the United States and Canada, and station snow depth where an official station is nearby. Units follow the device's region. The app is not offered in China mainland.

5. THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL
The app is not in a regulated industry. Its data is open data used under its licences, with credit shown in the app under "How the numbers are made" and at https://powtracker.app/terms.html: Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0), OpenStreetMap and OpenSkiMap (ODbL), government weather and snow agencies (public or open government licences), GeoSphere Austria and avalanche.report (CC BY 4.0). Season pass names (for example Ikon, Epic, Indy) appear only as factual labels for which mountains a pass covers; Powtracker is not affiliated with them.
